correctness.rationale: Banach-algebra logarithms are uniformly convergent for n>2C, and the computed first-order coefficient formula follows exactly. Absolute summation is justified by an l1 remainder, not pointwise approximations. DLMF verifies Bessel zero simplicity and distinct-order nonintersection; Bessel recurrences imply shifted signed roots c0(1-k)/(2n). The implicit-function theorem supplies local uniqueness, and the l1 directional derivative proves the full two-kink scaled norm profile. FFT and root-solving tests cover m=0,1,2,3 without being treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The two mathematically closest full primary texts address fixed pole parameters: Auxemery–Borichev–Zarouf (2026, Theorems 1–3, the explicit lambda>=1/2 witness split) and Szehr–Zarouf (2017, Theorem 1 and coefficient regions, constants depending on lambda). Neither stated result covers the double limit lambda=c/n or computes the order-1/n signed zero displacement and two-kink collision. NIST DLMF supplies standard Bessel identities/zeros, not this rational norm boundary layer. Targeted published-index and record searches returned no implication-equivalent result. Historical priority risk remains because search is not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Indexed retrieval is not proof of novelty; an unindexed equivalent shrinking-pole limit or signed coefficient-root asymptotic may predate this result.
Some mathematical sources are discoverable under different terminology; the substantive proof is independent of historical-priority assessment.

value.rationale: A natural rational witness used in a recent sharp Wiener-versus-Hardy inequality has a quantitatively different degeneration when its pole retreats at rate 1/n: bounded Wiener norm, infinitely many exact Bessel cusp thresholds and a previously unresolved asymmetric two-mode splitting scale m*c0/n. The complete local norm profile explains how a nondifferentiable limiting spectral invariant arises from two displaced Fourier zeros; the signed shifts are motivated by Fourier coefficient cancellation in this canonical rational family, not arbitrary parameter selection. It is explicitly not asserted to optimize the whole rational class.
